harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented VLAN segmentation over the shared node1-node2-node3 link using an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the ansible-controller managed node). node2 was placed on VLAN 10 (10.10.10.0/24) and node3 on VLAN 20 (10.10.20.0/24) via 802.1q sub-interfaces on their shared trunk NIC (enp8s0), configured with NetworkManager (community.general.nmcli). node1 (VyOS) was configured with matching eth1.10/eth1.20 sub-interfaces and routes traffic between the VLANs. End-to-end ping between node2 and node3 succeeds via node1 (TTL=63 confirms one router hop). The playbook is fully idempotent (repeat runs report changed=0). Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all four managed nodes: captured baseline boot IDs and healthy state, restarted each node one at a time via native reboot with an acknowledgement returned before disconnect, confirmed changed boot identity via /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, and verified full recovery of VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN connectivity after each restart — including a final idempotent Ansible re-run from the restarted control node (node4) proving the desired state persisted through every reboot.
actions_performed: Surveyed all four nodes' network config, OS, and Ansible tooling: node4 (Ubuntu 24.04, ansible-controller image with ansible-core, community.general, ansible.netcommon) is the control node; node1 is a VyOS router with eth0 (management) and eth1 (shared trunk); node2/node3 are RHEL10 with enp1s0 (management) and enp8s0 (shared trunk)

Established SSH access from node4 to all managed nodes: added node4's public key to VyOS user 'vyos' via 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' + commit/save on node1, and to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys on node2 and node3

Wrote /root/inventory.ini and /root/vlan-segmentation.yml on node4: a two-play Ansible playbook creating VLAN10/VLAN20 sub-interfaces + peer routes on node2/node3 via community.general.nmcli, and matching eth1.10/eth1.20 sub-interfaces on node1 via VyOS 'configure/set/commit/save' wrapped in bash -c, run with become:yes/sudo (required because VyOS's configure command fails to establish a config session over a non-interactive SSH exec without sudo)

Iterated on and fixed the playbook until a from-scratch reset-and-rerun produced full connectivity, then hardened it for idempotency (route-existence check, VyOS current-config check) so repeat runs report changed=0
Verified end-to-end routing: node2 (10.10.10.2) <-> node3 (10.10.20.2) via node1, confirmed by successful pings with TTL=63 (one router hop)
Captured pre-restart boot_id baselines and healthy-state evidence on node1, node2, node3, node4

Restarted node1 (VyOS 'reboot now', backgrounded with ack returned first), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified VLAN sub-interfaces/config persisted (VyOS 'save') and cross-VLAN ping still worked
Restarted node2 (native 'reboot', backgrounded), confirmed changed boot_id, verified vlan10 NetworkManager connection and route persisted and ping to node3 across the router worked
Restarted node3 (native 'reboot', backgrounded), confirmed changed boot_id, verified vlan20 connection/route persisted and ping to node2 across the router worked

Restarted node4 (native 'reboot', backgrounded), confirmed changed boot_id, verified ansible-playbook and the playbook/inventory files survived, and re-ran the playbook to prove it still converges to changed=0 (desired state fully persisted)
Ran final cross-VLAN ping test from node2 and node3 to confirm the fully-restarted cluster still routes between VLANs correctly

evidence.requirement: node2 placed on VLAN 10, node3 placed on VLAN 20 over the shared link
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook runs (using community.general.nmcli) created vlan10 on node2's enp8s0 trunk and vlan20 on node3's enp8s0 trunk; final idempotent run shows the VLAN connections already exist (ok, changed=0)

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between the VLANs so node2 and node3 can reach each other
evidence.summary: node1 shows eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24); node2 pings node3's VLAN IP (10.10.20.2) and node3 pings node2's VLAN IP (10.10.10.2) successfully with TTL=63, proving traffic transits node1

evidence.requirement: Implementation done via Ansible from the configured control node (node4)
evidence.summary: node4 identified as the ansible-controller managed node; /root/inventory.ini and /root/vlan-segmentation.yml authored there; ansible-playbook executed from node4 against node1/node2/node3 to apply all configuration
Re-run of the finalized playbook after fixes reports ok with changed=0 skipped=1/2 across all three managed hosts, confirming no further changes needed

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 50503c5d...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id changed to 8aa7f8be...; show interfaces confirms eth1.10/eth1.20 persisted and node2->node3 ping succeeds through node1

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id aad96cc9...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id changed to 9151dbd5...; vlan10 interface/route and ping to node3 (10.10.20.2) recovered successfully

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 180a78a0...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id changed to 4c6e79ff...; vlan20 interface/route and ping to node2 (10.10.10.2) recovered successfully

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6fd57414...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id changed to 07e5791a...; ansible-playbook and playbook/inventory files intact, re-run against the cluster shows changed=0 (fully converged/recovered)

evidence.requirement: Final post-recovery end-to-end connectivity across all restarted nodes
evidence.summary: After all four nodes were individually restarted and recovered, node2 and node3 still successfully ping each other's VLAN IPs across node1, confirming durable cross-VLAN routing
